blockMcqs.question: How does a player win Snake & Ladder?
options: By landing exactly on the last cell
By passing the last cell on any roll
By rolling the highest dice value
By avoiding all snakes for 10 turns
blockMcqs.explanation: The stated win condition is landing exactly on cell 100 — overshooting doesn't count.

blockMcqs.question: Which class owns the turn loop and player list?
options: Board
Dice
Game
Player
blockMcqs.explanation: Game coordinates the board, players, and dice, and runs the turn loop — it's the orchestrator.

blockMcqs.question: Why merge Snake and Ladder into one Jump class?
options: They differ only in start vs end direction
Ladders don't need a start cell
Snakes require inheritance to work
The board can't store two collections
blockMcqs.explanation: Both are just a start cell redirecting to an end cell; only whether end is above or below start differs, so one class covers both.

blockMcqs.question: In the Board pseudocode, what does resolve(cell) return?
options: Always the same cell unchanged
The jump's end cell if one exists there, else the cell itself
A random cell on the board
The board's total size
blockMcqs.explanation: resolve() looks up the cell in the jumps map and returns the redirected end cell, or the original cell if no jump exists.

blockMcqs.question: What data structure holds players in the Game class?
options: A stack
A sorted array
A queue
A binary tree
blockMcqs.explanation: Players are stored in a queue so turn order is just dequeue, play, and re-enqueue at the back.

blockMcqs.question: What happens if target exceeds the board size in playTurn?
options: The player moves to the last cell
The game throws an error
The move is skipped and turn ends
The player is removed from the queue
blockMcqs.explanation: playTurn() returns early on overshoot, leaving the player's position unchanged and ending their turn.

blockMcqs.question: Why avoid Snake and Ladder subclassing Jump?
options: Subclasses would need private constructors
Neither adds new fields or behavior over Jump
Inheritance is not supported in board games
Board can only store one subclass type
blockMcqs.explanation: Snake and Ladder would just be empty subclasses of Jump, adding two names without new state or behavior — composition is simpler.

blockMcqs.question: What future change does a separate Dice class enable?
options: Removing the board entirely
Swapping in a different dice strategy
Skipping the turn loop
Merging Player and Board classes
blockMcqs.explanation: Isolating Dice as its own class opens the door to the Strategy pattern, like swapping in a weighted or multi-dice variant.

blockMcqs.question: Why can't two jumps share the same start cell?
options: The rules forbid more than 10 jumps
A map keyed by cell can hold only one entry per key
Dice rolls prevent landing on shared cells
Players would win instantly
blockMcqs.explanation: Since jumps is a map keyed by the start cell, storing a second jump at the same key would just overwrite the first.

blockMcqs.question: Does landing at a ladder's top chain into another jump?
options: Yes, always chain until no jump remains
No, resolve() runs once per turn
Only for snakes, never ladders
Only if the player rolls a six
blockMcqs.explanation: The standard rule resolves at most one jump per turn, avoiding ambiguous chains of teleports.
